resolved_by: Sentencing Commission Amendment 786 (effective Nov. 1, 2014), which amended Application Note 1 to exclude 18 U.S.C. § 2250 from the definition of 'sex offense' in U.S.S.G. § 5D1.2.
issue: Is a failure-to-register conviction under 18 U.S.C. § 2250 a 'sex offense' for purposes of the Guidelines recommendation on the length of supervised release under U.S.S.G. § 5D1.2?

sides.position: Because failure to register is not a 'sex offense,' the Guidelines recommendation for supervised release is only the five-year minimum, not five years to life.
cases: United States v. Putnam, 806 F.3d 853 (5th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Floss, 42 F.4th 854 (8th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: The Guidelines range for supervised release in a failure-to-register case is five years to life, with the statutory maximum recommended.
cases: United States v. James, 792 F.3d 962 (8th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Floss, 42 F.4th 854 (8th Cir. 2022)

quote: In Amendment 786, effective November 1, 2014, the Sentencing Commission, to resolve a perceived circuit conflict, amended Application Note 1 to provide, "Such term does not include an offense under 18 U.S.C. § 2250 (Failure to register)."
cite: United States v. Brian Floss, 42 F.4th 854 (8th Cir. 2022)
